diagram:
flowchart TD
  SCHED["pg_cron · market-local slots\nUS DST-safe · India IST"] --> HOLD["Holdings first\nlive_account_snapshots ∪ paper_positions"]
  SCHED --> SCREEN["Dual-bucket screener\nfundamental momentum + value"]
  HOLD --> ROTATE["Staleness-ordered rotation\nunder ~105s wall-clock budget"]
  ROTATE --> COMPLETE["Completed daily sessions only\nUS 16:00 ET · India 15:30 IST"]
  SCREEN --> COMPLETE
  COMPLETE --> SCORE["Score available dimensions deterministically\nIndia news shadow is not scored"]
  SCORE --> WEIGHTS["Champion weights_snapshot\n→ PROFILE_WEIGHTS → literal · then tilt"]
  WEIGHTS --> ANALYST["analyst_score 0-100\navailability-masked + renormalized"]
  ANALYST --> GATE{"Deterministic direction gate\nLLM opinion never decides"}
  GATE -->|"held + below threshold"| SELLOK["short · exit signal"]
  GATE -->|"thin evidence <2 dims"| NEUTRAL["neutral · abstain"]
  GATE -->|"score ≥ mandate threshold"| LONG["long · new position"]
  SELLOK --> WRITE["Write agent_signals\nscore_source = deterministic_v1"]
  NEUTRAL --> WRITE
  LONG --> WRITE
  WRITE --> HANDOFF["PaperTrader\nmandate score_threshold · default 60"]

SCHED.label: pg_cron · US + India
SCHED.description: Separate per-market Supabase pg_cron jobs call Vercel. US 09:00 and 14:00 New York slots use paired EDT/EST UTC hours plus an exact local_slot guard; the seasonal duplicate exits before provider or DB work. India runs at fixed IST slots. Scores and directions are deterministic; the configured LLM writes optional narrative for new candidates only.
SCHED.addReason: Pre-market timing so signals are ready before open.
SCHED.changeReason: Model and mechanism were both false: the 2026-07-04 entry claimed Groq llama-3.3-70b under Windows Task Scheduler. Real model is per-flow config, default deepseek-reasoner; real scheduler is pg_cron with a separate India job.

HOLD.label: Holdings first
HOLD.description: Reads the union of the latest live_account_snapshots row per account/broker and open paper_positions (position_role='alpha') — it does NOT make a live Robinhood call, and it is not scoped to account 965848641. Snapshot capture was decoupled into its own endpoint, so this path only reads what that endpoint stored. Fails LOUD and never empty-on-error: a holdings read failure raises a critical 'research-holdings-fetch:<market>' issue and throws, because a silently-empty holdings list would look identical to 'you own nothing' and would silently drop every exit signal.
HOLD.addReason: Locked decision: holdings must be researched first; SELL signals allowed on owned positions.
HOLD.changeReason: Diagram claimed a live read-only Robinhood pull on account 965848641. That is not what runs: the source is live_account_snapshots ∪ paper_positions, and fetchAndStoreAccountSnapshot is explicitly no longer fired from this path. Fail-loud behaviour was undocumented.

ROTATE.label: Staleness-ordered rotation
ROTATE.description: Holdings are ordered by how long ago each was last scored (never-scored first) and worked through under a wall-clock budget. Held rows receive full deterministic scoring but skip optional LLM narrative and RAG retrieval. One existing worker is reserved for candidates while the others prioritize holdings, so discovery advances without raising concurrency. Deferred holdings raise an alert.
ROTATE.addReason: A fixed-order holdings loop under a timeout always starves the tail of the list; staleness ordering makes the truncation fair and the alert makes it honest.

COMPLETE.label: Completed daily sessions only
COMPLETE.description: After every provider fallback is normalized, ResearchAgent removes malformed/future bars and today's still-forming daily candle until the exchange regular close: 16:00 America/New_York or 15:30 Asia/Kolkata. The filtered series owns scoring, return capture, trade plans, and persisted observed evidence; chart/quote consumers remain free to use intraday data.
COMPLETE.addReason: Intraday research could otherwise score a mutable daily bar and compare it with settled historical bars.

SCREEN.label: Dual-bucket screener
SCREEN.description: Two buckets always run (no explicit regime switch), interleaved round-robin and capped at 6. US is a FinancialDatasets REST screener and is FUNDAMENTALS-ONLY: momentum = revenue_growth>0.15, earnings_growth>0.10, gross_margin>0.25, ROE>0.15, mcap>2B — a fundamental-momentum proxy, NOT price/RSI momentum. Value = absolute pe_ratio 0-18, FCF yield>0.04, debt_to_equity<1.0, mcap>1B — an absolute P/E cap, not sector-relative, and with no insider-buying filter. Price momentum (RSI>60, above 50DMA) exists only on the India leg, from india_screen_cache.
SCREEN.addReason: Regime adaptation emerges from scoring, not hardcoded bull/bear logic.
SCREEN.changeReason: The stated criteria described a screener that does not exist. The US leg has no RSI and no 50DMA filter at all, its P/E test is absolute rather than sector-median, and it has no insider-buying filter. Dual-bucket itself is accurate and unchanged.

SCORE.label: Score 5 dimensions
SCORE.description: The deterministic v1 vocabulary is fundamental, technical, sentiment, macro, and insider, but only structurally applicable and available dimensions enter a symbol's composite. India sentiment is now structurally excluded after GDELT produced 0/310 usable observations; NSE/Google replacement evidence is shadow-only. India macro is also unavailable. Options and analyst evidence are logged only and never weighted.
SCORE.addReason: Multi-dimensional scoring is the core of the strategy.
SCORE.changeReason: Node asserted the dimensions are 'combined by the current signal_weights' — false, and the exact class of claim this diagram exists to prevent. Weighting moved to its own WEIGHTS node. Also documented the insider cascade, the India macro exclusion, GDELT/FII-DII, and the availability mask, all of which shipped without a diagram update.

WEIGHTS.label: Champion-first weights
WEIGHTS.description: The legacy global signal_weights row is NO LONGER read on the scoring path. The real chain is: the per-market champion's weights_snapshot from strategy_versions (is_champion=true) → PROFILE_WEIGHTS[risk_profile] → a hardcoded literal, then applyStrategyTilt for the mandate's strategy_preference. Dimensions that are unavailable for a symbol (ETF fundamentals, technicals with <15 candles, India macro) are masked out and the surviving weights are renormalized, so an absent dimension shrinks the evidence base instead of silently scoring as average. signal_weights survives only as an Agents-page display row and a learner baseline — it moves nothing.
WEIGHTS.addReason: Split out of SCORE because the weighting source is exactly what the old diagram got wrong, and it is the seam where approved learning enters live scoring.

ANALYST.label: analyst_score
ANALYST.description: The 0-100 composite over the included dimensions only, with effective weights renormalized to the available evidence. Weights are tuned over time by the LearnerAgent, but only via a challenger the user promotes to champion — this node is where that approved learning is consumed.
ANALYST.changeReason: Verified accurate on the learning-loop claim; amended only to state that the composite is over included dimensions with renormalized weights, not over all five unconditionally.

GATE.label: Deterministic direction gate
GATE.description: Direction is decided by lib/signal-direction.ts, not by the model: the LLM's own direction opinion never influences the output and is kept advisory in raw_data._original_direction. Order matters — the held-and-below-threshold check runs FIRST, so a decayed holding still produces an exit even when its evidence has thinned. A separate degradation guard can only downgrade long→neutral, never suppress an exit, and currently ships measure-only unless explicitly set to enforce.
GATE.addReason: Replaces the old 'Held vs new?' node, which framed direction as a prompt/LLM outcome. It is a deterministic gate, and which check runs first is load-bearing for exits.

SELLOK.label: short · exit signal
SELLOK.description: A held name scoring below the mandate threshold is emitted as direction='short'. This branch is evaluated before the thin-evidence branch so that degraded evidence can never trap you in a position.
SELLOK.changeReason: Capability unchanged and still correct; restated in the code's own vocabulary (direction='short') and pinned to its precedence over the thin-evidence branch.

NEUTRAL.label: neutral · abstain
NEUTRAL.description: Fewer than 2 usable dimensions means the system abstains rather than guessing: direction='neutral', which the PaperTrader will not act on. Reached only for names that are not held-and-decayed.
NEUTRAL.addReason: The abstain path is a real, frequently-taken outcome and was invisible on the diagram — the old version drew only held/new.

LONG.label: long · new position
LONG.description: New candidates are long-only. There is NO 'top 3 per day' rule anywhere in the code: the real bounds are pre-scoring caps on candidate count — screener slice of 6, RESEARCH_CANDIDATE_CAP 40 (India 8) — with holdings exempt and overflow carried forward to the next run behind a backlog alert.
LONG.addReason: Long-only for new positions is a locked rule.
LONG.changeReason: 'Top 3/day by analyst_score' was false — no such cap exists in code, and the caps that do exist bound candidates BEFORE scoring rather than ranking after it. Long-only itself verified accurate and unchanged.

WRITE.label: Write agent_signals
WRITE.description: Persists direction, analyst_score, per-dimension scores, rationale, market, asset_class, mandate_id, and score_source='deterministic_v1' / scoring_version. Also writes research_packets, signal_score_history, decision_observations, pipeline_stage_events, and shadow_decisions.
WRITE.addReason: Signals are the durable output other agents consume.
WRITE.changeReason: Was accurate but incomplete. Added score_source, which is the field that structurally fences advisory LLM rows out of execution, plus the five companion tables this run writes.

HANDOFF.label: Handoff to PaperTrader
HANDOFF.description: PaperTrader selects pending, direction='long' signals at or above the MANDATE's per-market score_threshold — 60 is only the fallback default (horizon presets: short_swing 65, swing 60, position 58). It additionally requires a freshness cutoff and score_source='deterministic_v1' as a positive allowlist.
HANDOFF.changeReason: '≥60' was stated as the rule; it is a default. The threshold is mandate-driven per market and Settings-editable, and the handoff also filters on freshness and score_source, neither of which was drawn.

history.label: Completed-session and DST-safe scheduling remediation
history.reason: US slots now remain fixed in New York local time across EDT/EST, and provider-normalized daily bars cannot reach scoring until the relevant market session is complete. India GDELT scoring was retired; replacement news/event collection is shadow-only.

history.label: Cross-market scoring and capacity audit
history.reason: Held positions now persist is_holding=true, India and US watchlists are partitioned by authoritative market, research_enabled is honored, held rows skip optional LLM narrative, sentiment is sample-shrunk, and analyst targets are observation-only.

history.label: signal_weights is NOT the scoring path — champion-first is (WEIGHTS node added)
history.reason: The diagram asserted dimensions are 'combined by the current signal_weights'. Code says the opposite in its own comment: the legacy global signal_weights row is NO LONGER read on the scoring path; it was an unreachable third fallback and survives only as an Agents-page display row and a learner baseline. The live chain is per-market champion weights_snapshot (strategy_versions, is_champion=true) → PROFILE_WEIGHTS[risk_profile] → hardcoded literal, then applyStrategyTilt for the mandate's strategy_preference. This was not a wording nit: the diagram pointed a reader at a table they could edit with zero effect on scoring, while hiding the champion promotion that is the ONLY way learning reaches live money. Split into a dedicated WEIGHTS node rather than patched inline, because the weighting source is the single most load-bearing claim on this page. Also recorded the availability mask + renormalization that ships with it: unavailable dimensions are excluded and surviving weights renormalize, so absent evidence shrinks the base instead of scoring as a silent 50.

history.label: Model was Groq llama-3.3-70b, is per-flow DeepSeek; scheduler was never Windows Task Scheduler
history.reason: The 2026-07-04 history entry recorded a 'correction' to Groq llama-3.3-70b that was itself wrong, so the diagram has been confidently lying for two weeks. Real model: getConfiguredModel(supabase,'research','deepseek-reasoner') — per-flow from Settings via agent_config, prod row deepseek-reasoner. Groq appears in the LLM router only as a generic dispatch branch and is never named for research. Real scheduler: Supabase pg_cron calling the Vercel route over HTTP (kairos-research 0 13 * * 1-5), plus a SECOND India job (kairos-research-india, realigned to 0 4 * * 1-5 by migration 082) that the single-schedule diagram never showed. Also recorded that the LLM writes the thesis narrative ONLY — every score is deterministic before the model is called — which is the inverse of what a 'model runs the scoring pass' reading implies.

history.label: Direction is a deterministic gate, not an LLM opinion (NEUTRAL abstain path drawn)
history.reason: The old LONGONLY 'Held vs new?' node framed direction as an outcome of the research prompt. It is not: lib/signal-direction.ts decides, and the LLM's direction opinion NEVER influences the output — it is retained advisory-only in raw_data._original_direction. Three branches now drawn where the diagram drew two. held + analyst_score < threshold → 'short'; thin evidence (<2 usable dimensions) → 'neutral' abstain; else score ≥ threshold → 'long'. Branch ORDER is itself load-bearing and now documented: the held-and-below-threshold check runs BEFORE the thin-evidence check, so a decayed holding still exits rather than being trapped by its own thinning evidence. The abstain path was previously invisible despite being a real and frequent outcome. The evidence-degradation guard is noted as measure-only and one-directional (can downgrade long→neutral, can never suppress an exit).

history.label: Holdings staleness-ordered rotation under wall-clock budget + deferred-holdings alert
history.reason: Shipped since 2026-07-04 and entirely absent from the diagram. Holdings are ordered by last-scored age (never-scored first) and processed under RESEARCH_BUDGET_MS (~105s), with names that fall off the end raising a deferred-holdings alert. Drawn as its own node because it changes what a truncated run MEANS: without it, a slow-provider day silently re-scores the same head of the list forever and starves the tail; with it, truncation is fair and visible. Paired with the fail-loud fetchHoldings note on HOLD — a holdings read failure raises a critical issue and throws rather than returning [], because an empty list is indistinguishable from 'you own nothing' and would silently drop every exit signal.

history.label: Source is live_account_snapshots ∪ paper_positions — not a live RH call on 965848641
history.reason: Diagram claimed it 'pulls current Robinhood positions (read-only, account 965848641) BEFORE screening'. Code reads the latest live_account_snapshots row per account/broker unioned with open paper_positions (position_role='alpha'); 965848641 appears only in the snapshot-capture endpoint, which gatherSymbols explicitly no longer calls (decoupled). The distinction matters operationally: holdings freshness is now a property of the snapshot job, not of this run, so a stalled snapshot job silently ages the holdings this agent researches — invisible under the old description. Holdings-first priority and SELL-on-holdings are verified accurate and unchanged.

history.label: 'Top 3/day by analyst_score' does not exist — caps are pre-scoring on candidate count
history.reason: No 3/day cap exists anywhere in the code. Real bounds: screener returns .slice(0,6); RESEARCH_CANDIDATE_CAP default 40 (India 8); holdings are cap-EXEMPT; overflow is carried forward to the next run behind a backlog alert. The difference is not cosmetic — 'top 3 by analyst_score' describes ranking AFTER scoring, while the real caps bound the candidate list BEFORE scoring, so the system never learns what the names it dropped would have scored. Long-only enforcement on new positions is verified accurate and unchanged. Note the CLAUDE.md locked rule still says 'screener target: 3 candidates/day'; the code's screener cap is 6 — flagged as a rule/code divergence, not resolved here.

history.label: US screener is fundamentals-only — no RSI, no 50DMA, absolute P/E, no insider filter
history.reason: Momentum was described as 'RSI>60, price>50DMA, revenue accel' and Value as 'P/E<sector median … insider buying'. The US leg is a FinancialDatasets REST screener with no price data at all: momentum is revenue_growth>0.15 / earnings_growth>0.10 / gross_margin>0.25 / ROE>0.15 — a fundamental-momentum proxy the code names as such — and value uses an ABSOLUTE pe_ratio 0-18 cap with no sector comparison and no insider-buying filter. RSI>60 / above-50DMA exist only on the India leg via india_screen_cache. Dual-bucket-always-on verified accurate and unchanged; only the criteria moved.

history.label: ≥60 is a mandate default, not the rule; freshness + deterministic_v1 allowlist added
history.reason: The handoff threshold is trading_mandates.score_threshold per market (horizon presets: short_swing 65, swing 60, position 58); 60 is only the ?? fallback. Research and PaperTrader read the same mandate source, so the number is Settings-editable and can differ US vs India — a hardcoded '≥60' on the diagram would send a reader to change the wrong thing. Also drew the two filters the handoff has always applied but the diagram never showed: a signal freshness cutoff, and score_source='deterministic_v1' as a POSITIVE allowlist (a negative filter would fail open and let advisory LLM rows reach fills).

history.label: 'Held vs new?' decision node removed, superseded by GATE
history.reason: Removed rather than edited. The node framed the held/new split as the decision, when the real decision is a three-branch deterministic gate whose thin-evidence abstain path the old node could not express and whose branch ordering it actively obscured. Kept as a removal record rather than a silent deletion so the shape change is auditable.

history.label: Verified accurate — champion/promotion claim unchanged
history.reason: 'Weights are tuned over time by the LearnerAgent (via promoted challengers)' is TRUE and matches the code comment at the champion read: LearnerAgent proposes weight challengers → user promotes one to champion → this is where that approved learning gets consumed. Only amendment: the composite is over INCLUDED dimensions with renormalized effective weights, not over all five unconditionally. No churn invented.
